name: John Wesley

died.place: Chapel-house beside City Road Chapel, City Road, London, England

life_summary: John Wesley was born in 1703 at Epworth Rectory in Lincolnshire, a son of the rector Samuel Wesley and his wife Susanna, and was educated at Charterhouse School and Christ Church, Oxford. He was ordained deacon in 1725 and priest in 1728, was elected a fellow of Lincoln College in 1726, served as his father's curate, mainly at Wroot, from 1727 to 1729, and from November 1729 led the Oxford group nicknamed the Holy Club or "Methodists". In 1735 he sailed to Georgia as a missionary and ministered at Savannah from February 1736 until December 1737, when he left after legal proceedings that followed his refusal of communion to Sophia Williamson (née Hopkey). Back in London, he recorded that on 24 May 1738, at a society meeting in Aldersgate Street, his heart was "strangely warmed", and from April 1739 he took up open-air preaching, beginning at Bristol. For the next five decades he travelled through England, Wales, Ireland and Scotland as an itinerant preacher, organised societies, presided over annual conferences of preachers from 1744 and published Sermons on Several Occasions (1746–1760). His 1751 marriage to the widow Mary Vazeille was childless and ended in separation, and in 1784 he gave the Methodist Conference legal standing by the Deed of Declaration and ordained preachers for America. He died at his house beside City Road Chapel, London, on 2 March 1791, aged 87.

phases.label: Epworth and Charterhouse
phases.summary: Childhood at Epworth Rectory, Lincolnshire, where his father Samuel was rector; he was rescued from the rectory fire of February 1709. From January 1714 he was a pupil on the foundation at Charterhouse School in London.

phases.label: Oxford student and fellow
phases.summary: Student at Christ Church, Oxford, from June 1720 (BA 1724); ordained deacon in September 1725 and elected fellow of Lincoln College in March 1726, where he was chosen Greek lecturer and moderator of the classes.

phases.label: Curate at Wroot
phases.summary: From August 1727 he served as his father's curate, living and officiating mainly at Wroot near Epworth, while keeping his Lincoln fellowship. He was ordained priest in September 1728 and was recalled to Oxford by a letter from the rector of Lincoln in October 1729.

phases.label: Holy Club at Oxford
phases.summary: Resident fellow and tutor at Lincoln College from November 1729, leading the small society nicknamed the Holy Club or Methodists, which from August 1730 visited prisoners in Oxford. He declined to seek his father's Epworth living; his father died in April 1735.

sources.label: John Telford, The Life of John Wesley, ch. 5 (Wesley Center Online)

phases.label: Georgia mission
phases.summary: Missionary to the colony of Georgia with his brother Charles; he embarked in October 1735, ministered at Savannah from February 1736, and left on 2 December 1737 after the dispute over Sophia Williamson, landing at Deal on 1 February 1738.

sources.label: John Telford, The Life of John Wesley, ch. 6 (Wesley Center Online)

phases.label: Aldersgate and field preaching
phases.summary: After his Aldersgate experience (May 1738) and a visit to the Moravians at Herrnhut (August 1738), he began open-air preaching at Bristol in April 1739, laid the foundation of the New Room there and made the Foundery his London base. He extended his work to Newcastle in 1742.

phases.label: Itinerant leader of Methodism
phases.summary: Based at the Foundery in London, he presided over annual conferences from 1744 and travelled continually through England, Wales, Ireland (from 1747) and Scotland (from 1751), publishing Sermons on Several Occasions (1746–1760). He married Mary Vazeille in 1751, resigned his fellowship that June, fell seriously ill in 1753, and his wife finally left him in 1776.
phases.place: London (the Foundery); Bristol; Newcastle; itinerant tours

phases.label: City Road final years
phases.summary: His London headquarters moved to the new City Road Chapel (opened November 1778), and he lived in the adjoining house from 1779 to 1791. In these years his wife died (1781), he secured the Conference legally and ordained preachers for America (1784), made his last Irish visit (1789) and preached in the open air for the last time in October 1790.

corrections: Wednesbury riot event (20 Oct 1743): changed 'at night ... carried to Walsall and back for several hours' to the sourced account (seized in the evening, taken to Bentley Hall and Walsall, about five hours, returned to Wednesbury); added Telford ch. 12 as a second source.

'Scriptural Christianity' event (24 Aug 1744): 'it was his last university sermon there' restated as Wesley's own expectation ('he supposed it was his last time'), sourced to the University Church of St Mary the Virgin page, which replaces the DNB citation (the DNB does not support this claim).
Open-air preaching event (2 Apr 1739): changed 'at Whitefield's urging ... near Bristol' to 'at Whitefield's invitation ... on ground adjoining Bristol' to match Telford and the DNB.

Birth and fire events: replaced the Methodist Heritage citation, which gives only the year, with the Westminster Abbey page (birth) and the Epworth Old Rectory page (9 Feb 1709 fire), which give exact dates.
Death event: replaced the second citation (Telford ch. 21, which is vague on the burial vault) with the Westminster Abbey page, which confirms 2 March death and 9 March burial.
Curate at Wroot phase and 1729 event: 'recalled by his college' made precise as recalled by the rector of Lincoln (Morley's letter of 21 Oct 1729, per DNB).
Holy Club phase: prison visiting date narrowed from '1730' to 'August 1730' (Telford: 24 Aug 1730).
Georgia phase: 'sailed in late 1735' changed to 'embarked in October 1735' (Gravesend, 14 Oct 1735; the voyage from Cowes began 10 Dec), and the departure date of 2 December 1737 was added.
Georgia departure event: added that the communion refusal happened in August 1737 (Telford: 7 Aug).
Aldersgate phase: 'built the New Room' changed to 'laid the foundation of the New Room' (foundation stone 12 May 1739), and the Herrnhut visit dated to August 1738.
Itinerant phase: added his June 1751 resignation of the fellowship and his wife's final departure in 1776 (DNB).

City Road phase: vague 'kept travelling until 1790' replaced with the sourced facts: last Irish visit in 1789 and last open-air sermon in October 1790 (Telford ch. 21); house residence dated 1779–1791; Telford ch. 18 added as a source.
Wife's death event: 'he was away travelling' replaced with his own account that he learned of it on reaching London on 14 October (Telford ch. 15).
Fellowship event: added the exact resignation date, 1 June 1751 (DNB).
Top-level sources: replaced the single-journal-month citation with the Westminster Abbey page.
